title: An abrupt silicon PN junction
shows: Acceptors 2e21 and donors 1e21 per m³ in silicon (n_i = 1e16 per m³, 300 K): the built-in potential is V_T·ln(N_A·N_D/n_i²) = 0.6132 V. Forward biased, the current grows as exp(V/(n·V_T)) with an ideality n near 1: from 0.3 to 0.4 V by between e^(0.1/(1.02·V_T)) and e^(0.1/V_T) = 47.9 times. Reverse biased, its depletion capacitance is A·√(qεN_AN_D / (2(N_A+N_D)(V_bi − V − 2V_T))): 0.0465 fF at −2 V and 0.0595 fF at −1 V. 10 µm long on 401 nodes, so the depletion stays clear of the contacts.
source: Abrupt junction and the ideal diode law: S. M. Sze and K. K. Ng, Physics of Semiconductor Devices, 3rd ed. (2007), §2.2 and §2.3.

checks.what: current at 0.4 V over the current at 0.3 V
